entry.title: UI polish + reliability: undo, scroll hygiene, async reading generation
entry.content:
UI polish + reliability: undo, scroll hygiene, async reading generation

Undo (regressed a few times):
- one tap = back to the previous card, always exactly one. History entries to
  revert are claimed synchronously before any await (a concurrent/ghost tap
  can't grab the same ones); a failed-then-passed card (two history rows) peels
  in one tap. 4 node tests + a server-side undo_last sequence test.

Scroll / chrome:
- overscroll-behavior:none on html/body kills the browser pull-to-refresh that
  showed a scrollbar but never refreshed.
- scrollbars hidden app-wide (everything is touch-scrolled) — no more stray bar
  under the stats tabs or in sheets.
- min-height:0 + overscroll-behavior:contain on every in-app scroll region, so a
  flex child actually scrolls instead of overflowing (reading mode scroll).
- the reading "review" strip sits under the studybar instead of on top of it.
- flow sheets get a top "‹ back"; textarea tall enough for its placeholder.

Reading generation:
- create() returns immediately and builds the plan + first part on a background
  thread; the client polls chunks/last and shows "planning… / writing…" instead
  of a frozen "writing your first page" that timed out.
- the plan call (structure only) moved to haiku.

entry.title: TTS: Piper neural voice as the default
entry.content:
TTS: Piper neural voice as the default

Local neural TTS (piper-tts + onnxruntime, ~real-time on CPU). The big win over
Apple `say` / Milena: espeak-ng phonemisation respects the U+0301 stress marks
the app already carries, so Russian stress comes out right.

- tts_hq backend priority: elevenlabs > piper > apple `say` > silero. Auto-used
  whenever a ru_RU-*.onnx model is present in ~/Library/Application Support/
  ru-anki/piper/ (not committed; `python -m piper.download_voices`).
- _piper_synth keeps the stress marks; falls back to `say` then silero on any
  error. RU_TTS_PIPER_VOICE / RU_TTS_PIPER_LENGTH to tune.
- Speech Lab "Free · local" button now selects piper; cleared cached reading /
  speech audio so it regenerates with the new voice.

entry.title: Reading: mark every inflected form of tapped and carded words
entry.content:
Reading: mark every inflected form of tapped and carded words

The old surface-string matching only lit up words in nearly the same form as one
you'd tapped or carded — too strict.

- reading_flow._mark_words lemmatises every word in the chunks server-side and
  returns a surface->lemma map plus which lemmas are tapped-this-session vs
  already-carded. In the chunk and session payloads.
- Frontend: a tapped word is highlighted in ALL its forms; a word you already
  had a card for (and haven't tapped) is underlined in all its forms — a chance
  to recall it in context. Both visible at once.
- Tapping an underlined word peeks at the card's meaning without counting it as
  unknown; "still don't know it" converts it to a real tap.

entry.title: SRS: floor the interval when you pass a card
entry.content:
SRS: floor the interval when you pass a card

FSRS grinds a repeatedly-failed card down to a sub-day stability, then schedules
both Good and Easy for tomorrow — identical intervals that feel broken and bury
you in reviews the next day.

- srs._floor_pass: passing a graduated card (Good/Easy) now always buys at least
  MIN_GOOD_DAYS (2) / MIN_EASY_DAYS (4), and nudges the card's stability up to
  match so the schedule stays self-consistent. The floor only bites when FSRS
  would give less; healthy cards are untouched.
- Applied in review(), preview() (so the buttons show the real numbers), and on
  the final state of rebuild_schedule replays.
- One-shot rebuild lifted 84 live cards off <2d; state-2 cards under 1d: 76 -> 0.

entry.title: SRS: full honest replay to repair the state-reset corruption
entry.content:
SRS: full honest replay to repair the state-reset corruption

~35 cards were reset on Sept 5 to stability=3.0 / difficulty=6.5 (not FSRS
values) with due/last_review kept, wiping their lapse history — then a Good/Easy
inflated them to a 7-11 day interval they hadn't earned. Meanwhile the
early-review bug had crushed many older cards to ~1 day.

- rebuild_all_schedules() now replays every reviewed card's log through FSRS on
  an honest schedule (no review scored as early), collapsing runs of "Again"
  within an hour — drilling a card back in is not repeated failure.
- Cards carrying the 3.0/6.5 fingerprint get the honest value even if that means
  a shorter interval (they were inflated); repaired ids are recorded so they're
  not re-touched. Every other card can only grow — a healthy card is never
  shortened by a determinism difference in the replay.
- daily_healthcheck detects the fingerprint going forward.
- Live: 114 cards grew (avg +12d stability), 24 shrank; projected daily reviews
  dropped from ~198 to ~94.

entry.title: SRS: multi-factor new-card priority + a backlog triage screen
entry.content:
SRS: multi-factor new-card priority + a backlog triage screen

Pure frequency/creation order meant classic-fiction vocabulary never got
introduced and cards were surfaced weeks after their context went cold.

- srs_cards.priority (0-100) + priority_meta: a weighted blend of speaking use,
  daily-life use, and classic-literature use (LLM card_priority, one batched
  call), overall frequency rank, Anna Karenina appearance, and recency of
  creation (12-day halflife). Weights live in app_settings.new_card_weights
  (GET/POST /srs/new-card-weights) and can be re-applied without an LLM call
  (rescore_priorities_from_meta). _NEW_ORDER is now priority-first.
- The daily pass scores new cards with card_priority and re-blends existing
  priorities so the recency factor drifts.
- Triage: GET /srs/new-triage (worst-priority first, with the score breakdown),
  POST /srs/cards/bulk {ids, suspend|delete}. New #triageView screen opened from
  the "N new cards queued" home strip — see each card's speak/daily/fiction/
  freq/recency scores and park or delete the bottom of the pile.

entry.title: SRS: fix the early-review stability trap + add a daily schedule healt…
entry.content:
SRS: fix the early-review stability trap + add a daily schedule healthcheck

The daily batch surfaces every graduated card hours before its due date. FSRS
reads an early review as "almost no time elapsed" and barely grows stability, so
the whole collection was trapped near a 1-day interval — Good and Easy both
showed "1d" on cards seen for days.

- srs._on_schedule_time(): a review of a card that was due within today's batch
  window but done early is scored as if it happened on the due date (review() and
  preview()). A failed review, or one done far ahead of the batch, still counts
  as early so reviewing ahead isn't rewarded.
- rebuild_schedule() / rebuild_all_schedules() + POST /srs/rebuild-schedules:
  replay a flattened card's review log on an honest schedule to restore the
  stability it earned. Repaired ~69 live cards.
- srs.daily_healthcheck() runs once a day when the next day's cards are decided
  (also POST /srs/healthcheck): catches FSRS state wipes, impossible/flattened
  schedules, and a projected review spike vs the recent daily rate; auto-repairs
  what it safely can; report shown as a banner on the Reviews stats tab.
- ~7 cards had their FSRS state wiped ~Sept 1 (due forced to 2026-09-01T00:00:00)
  — root cause unconfirmed; the healthcheck now catches that class.

entry.title: Reading: manual next-part generation; ease into historical fiction
entry.content:
Reading: manual next-part generation; ease into historical fiction

- Generating the next part is now an explicit tap of "continue reading" —
  scrolling never triggers it (flowWireScroll no longer observes; flowMaybeMore
  is a no-op). Reading past a part without marking words was feeding the level
  estimate a false "understood it all" signal.
- proficiency.note_session skips the global known_rank blend when the session
  has zero taps (ambiguous: comprehension vs. skimming). _retune likewise holds
  rank_est steady on zero taps instead of raising it.
- fiction: target novel-vocab ramps by part (1,2,2,3,3) with the slice growing
  from the front so early words recur; a per-part PACING note keeps the opening
  parts near the reader's level; the FORM palette is capped at ~2 new period
  words per part (was "1-2 per paragraph") and told to reuse earlier ones.

entry.title: Activate: speaking-level ladder, self-adjusting difficulty, calibrati…
entry.content:
Activate: speaking-level ladder, self-adjusting difficulty, calibration sweep

- speaking_levels.py: per-CEFR productive-vocab bands; speaking level on the
  same 0..6 scale as reading; the gap tracked in proficiency_snapshots and
  rendered on the Level tab (profSpeaking + profDualSpark).
- CEFR difficulty a1..c2; self-adjusts to hold ~85% success (the "85% rule"),
  jumps 2 rungs on a perfect streak; manual slider + auto toggle.
- _hardness scores each verb 0..4 off its primary government pattern; the
  traps (bare instr/gen, unpredictable prep) are introduced first.
- endless: per_day 0 = unlimited; next_item never dead-ends.
- diagnostic sentences: everything around the target stays lexically trivial
  so a failure implicates the target.
- granular failure tags (activate_log.categories) feed weak_spots; typed-check
  moved to /activate/items/{id}/check (no double-log).
- calibration sweep (/activate/calibrate): retire verbs whose government you
  already handle — fast baseline for a big passive vocabulary.
- fixed a CSS rule that broke the settings slider + auto toggle.
- home screen: primary modes are two big tiles (Speak / Read).
- LEARNING.md: the 85% rule + diagnostic task design (principles 13, 14).

entry.title: Speaking activation: verb-government gym + productive-vocabulary drill
entry.content:
Speaking activation: verb-government gym + productive-vocabulary drill

New silent, phone-first mode (app/activate.py) for turning passive vocabulary
active — the biggest gap between the learner's reading (B2+/C1−) and speaking
(A2/B1). One mode, two tracks:

- verb: a high-frequency verb + its GOVERNMENT (which case/preposition each
  argument takes). Curriculum: app/data/activate/verbs.json.gz — the 220 most
  common verbs, each with 1–3 argument patterns + example + the trap an English
  speaker falls into (built by build_activate_verbs.py). The learner's stated #1
  weakness.
- word: a common content word, introduced newest-frequent-first from the freq
  list.

Loop: app names a target + a concrete personalised thought to express; learner
forms the Russian in their head (reveal + self-grade) or types it (focused LLM
check — is the government right? one more fix, nothing else). SM-2-lite spacing;
prompt angle varies each time an item recurs. `mix` setting weights verbs/words
(default 0.65, heavy verbs early); `level` = gentle/standard/stretch.

/activate/{next,items/{id}/grade,stats,settings}. Active-word count on the Level
tab next to passive known_words, tracked daily (proficiency_snapshots.active_words).
See LEARNING.md. Frames (track 3) still to come.
